properties.decision: circular_dependency drops from Critical to Warning when BOTH hold: no hop of the loop is a real DEPENDS_ON edge, and every Interface it runs through carries a foundation medium (`library` or `data`). Any real DEPENDS_ON edge anywhere in the loop keeps the whole cycle Critical, and an `unspecified` medium never earns the downgrade.
properties.name: A dependency cycle running only through file and library contracts is a Warning, not a Critical
properties.rationale:
Anthony's call, 2026-08-01, from three options. `Critical` means MUST FIX, and a loop that exists only because two parts read and write the same file formats has nothing to fix — a renderer that reads MIDI and writes WAV against a transcriber doing the reverse has no runtime dependency in either direction, and either runs on a machine where the other does not exist. Four such loops were reported `critical` in a single adopt pass over an ~11k-LOC repo and NONE was real, on the detector the adopt skill sells as the payoff of a brownfield pass.

DOWNGRADED, NOT SILENCED, and that distinction was the decision. Option (c), suppressing the case entirely, was rejected because shared-data coupling is sometimes genuine — two services over one table can be truly entangled, since a schema change in one breaks the other — so the finding keeps its place, its affected set, its suggested fix and its explanation, and loses only the claim that it is an emergency. Option (a), leaving Critical and relying on the improved message from BL-141(a), was rejected because a severity is a claim about what the reader should DO: prose cannot repair a wrong word, and a severity cannot be filtered on if it is wrong four times out of four.

TWO GUARDS MAKE THIS SAFE RATHER THAN QUIET. `contracts_only` is the load-bearing one — a single genuine DEPENDS_ON edge in the loop is a real dependency and does not stop being one by sharing a loop with a data contract. And `Interface.medium` defaults to `unspecified`, which is NOT a foundation medium, so silence about the medium keeps the louder answer; a design that never classified its boundaries is not quietly excused. Both are pinned by their own cases and both mutations are caught: dropping the contracts_only guard fails exactly the mixed-cycle test, and downgrading every cycle fails FOUR tests including the pre-existing one that has asserted Critical since the detector was written.

THE PRECEDENT WAS NOT LEANED ON. `is_foundation_medium` already exempts library/data from single_point_of_failure, but on grounds that do not transfer — 'you cannot run a second copy of it, so add_redundancy is incoherent' is an argument about whether a FIX is possible, not about whether a DEPENDENCY exists. This decision stands on its own reasoning.

VERIFIED ON THE ORIGINATING PROJECT'S REAL DATA: their reported loop, cmp:fundamental-detection → cmp:midi-renderer → cmp:fundamental-detection through ifc:midi-file and ifc:wav-audio (both `data`), now reports WARNING with its explanation intact.
